title: World Traveler Words
kidRule: English has borrowed words from languages all over the world, like Spanish, German, and Hindi. They often keep a little of their home spelling, so we learn each word's special part.
hint: This word traveled into English from another language, so it may not follow our usual rules. Say each beat slowly. Which part sounds surprising?
reminder: Borrowed words keep the spelling from their home language. Say the word in beats and remember its special part. Many Spanish words end in O or A!

check.question: Why does PATIO end with the letter O?
check.correctAnswer: It came from Spanish, and many Spanish words end in O or A!
distractors: Because all outdoor words end with the letter O
Because the O is silent and is only there for decoration

words.def: A flat outdoor space next to a house where people sit, eat, or play.
words.sent: We ate lunch outside on the patio.
words.story: This word is Spanish. In Spain, it is the name for a courtyard inside a house that is open to the sky!
words.card: I gave the dog a *pat* on the *patio*, and he did a happy flip!

words.def: A salty baked snack twisted into a knot shape.
words.sent: I bought a warm, salty pretzel at the fair.
words.story: This word comes from German. An old story says the twisted shape was made to look like folded arms!
words.card: What a *pret*ty *pretzel*, twisted up like a sleepy snake!

words.def: Soft, comfy clothes that you wear to bed.
words.sent: I put on my pajamas and brushed my teeth.
words.story: This word came from India, where it was the name for loose, comfy trousers. Long ago it meant 'leg clothing'!
words.card: I spilled strawberry *jam* on my dinosaur *pajamas*!

words.def: A sweet brown treat made from roasted cacao beans.
words.sent: I stirred chocolate into my warm milk.
words.story: This word came through Spanish from the Aztec people of Mexico, who made a spicy, bitter drink from cacao beans!
words.card: The sloth was *late* because it stopped for hot *chocolate*!

words.def: A big reptile with a long tail, a wide snout, and lots of teeth that lives in swamps and rivers.
words.sent: An alligator floated like a log in the swamp.
words.story: This word comes from the Spanish words 'el lagarto', which mean 'the lizard'!
words.card: *All* day the *alligator* practiced smiling for picture day!

words.def: A small flying insect that bites and leaves an itchy bump.
words.sent: A mosquito buzzed around my tent all night.
words.story: In Spanish, mosquito means 'little fly'. Only the females bite!
words.card: The *mosquito* would not *quit* buzzing songs in my ear!

words.def: Liquid soap for washing your hair.
words.sent: The shampoo made a mountain of bubbles on my head.
words.story: This word comes from a Hindi word that means 'to press or rub', just like rubbing your head when you wash it!
words.card: At c*amp*, the bear washed his fur with blueberry *shampoo*!

words.def: A trip to see wild animals where they live, especially in Africa.
words.sent: We saw zebras and lions on our safari.
words.story: This is a word from Swahili, a language of East Africa, where it means 'journey'!
words.card: We drove so *far* on *safari* that a giraffe asked for a ride!

words.def: The school class for young children, just before first grade.
words.sent: My little brother starts kindergarten in the fall.
words.story: This word is German for 'children's garden'. A teacher named Friedrich Froebel started the very first one in Germany almost 200 years ago!
words.card: A *kind* dragon came to *kindergarten* and shared his crayons!

words.def: A thin, round, flat bread made from corn or wheat.
words.sent: I rolled beans and rice inside a warm tortilla.
words.story: In Spanish, this word means 'little cake', and in Spanish the double L says /y/!
words.card: Wait un*til* the *tortilla* stops spinning like a flying saucer!
